cleanIntro: The Model P is a Colt-pattern single action: fixed cylinder turning on a base pin, one chamber at a time visible through the loading gate, and a hammer with four positions rather than a safety catch. Cleaning it starts with the same motion loading it does — hammer to half cock, gate open, cylinder turned a full revolution under your eye. The one thing to establish before you touch the base pin is which frame you have, because Uberti builds this revolver two ways and the pin is released differently on each.

steps.title: Whose book this is
steps.action: Read this guide knowing where its words come from. The book is published by Uberti, who build this revolver, and it addresses your revolver as a Uberti single action throughout — the cover lists the whole family it covers, Model P first. Cimarron distributes it as the manual for its single actions and adds a separate two-page safety sheet of its own; nothing in that sheet replaces a procedure here.
steps.prose: Cimarron's own sheet is worth having beside you: it is where the distributor states which frame types it sells and how each one's base pin is released.
steps.aside: The running text reads: "READ ALL INSTRUCTIONS AND WARNINGS. BEFORE USING YOUR UBERTI SINGLE ACTION FIREARM, CAREFULLY READ AND UNDERSTAND ALL OF THE WARNINGS, INSTRUCTIONS AND OTHER INFORMATION IN THIS MANUAL."
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — UNKNOWN — no revision or part code printed — Cover, printed p.1 (the cover's display type extracts with its spaces lost)

steps.title: A fixed cylinder means you check one chamber at a time
steps.action: Understand what you are about to inspect. Unlike a swing-out revolver, nothing on this gun opens to show you all six chambers at once — the cylinder is fixed and turns on the base pin, and only the chamber lined up with the loading gate can be seen. That is why every check on this revolver is a full revolution of the cylinder, not a glance.
steps.prose: Six chambers, one window. If you did not turn it all the way round, you did not check it.
steps.quote: Unlike modern revolvers, which provide for the entire cylinder to rotate away from the frame exposing all bores or chambers, this single action revolver has a fixed cylinder which rotates around the cylinder base pin.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — UNKNOWN — no revision or part code printed — General Operation and Nomenclature, printed p.4
steps.warn: ALWAYS KEEP AN EMPTY CHAMBER BELOW THE HAMMER DURING TRANSPORTATION OR STORAGE.

steps.title: Unload with the ejector rod — full stroke, every chamber
steps.action: Bring the hammer back to half cock and open the loading gate fully. Push the ejector rod under the barrel back toward the cylinder to drive the cartridge or case out through the gate, let the rod return, turn the cylinder to the next chamber and repeat. Use the rod's whole travel each time — a short stroke leaves a case half out where it jams the cylinder.
steps.prose: The cylinder should turn freely with the gate open and the hammer at half cock. If it will not, stop and find out why before forcing it.
steps.quote: You must operate the ejector rod its full length in each chamber to ensure complete cartridge ejection.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — UNKNOWN — no revision or part code printed — Unloading, printed p.11
steps.warn: Move the hammer rearward to the half cock (loading) position and open the loading gate fully.

steps.title: One more full revolution before anything comes apart
steps.action: With the hammer at half cock and the gate open, turn the cylinder slowly through one complete revolution and look into each of the six chambers in turn. Only when all six have been seen empty does cleaning start. This is a separate check from the unloading you just did, and the manual asks for it separately on purpose.
steps.prose: The gun cannot show you all six at once, so the only proof is having looked at each one. Do it under a light.
steps.quote: Before beginning any cleaning or maintenance procedures, MAKE SURE the revolver is unloaded.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — UNKNOWN — no revision or part code printed — Cleaning and Maintenance, printed p.11
steps.warn: Failure to follow this step could lead to SERIOUS INJURY OR DEATH.

steps.title: Gate open, hammer at half cock
steps.action: The cylinder comes out with the gun in the loading state, not at rest. Open the loading gate and bring the hammer rearward to half cock so the bolt drops out of the cylinder notches and the cylinder is free to turn.
steps.prose: At half cock the cylinder is unlocked but the hammer is caught. That is the only position this works from.
steps.quote: REMOVING THE CYLINDER: To remove the cylinder, follow these steps: 1. Open the loading gate. 2. Move the hammer rearward to the half cock (loading) position.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — UNKNOWN — no revision or part code printed — Removing the Cylinder, printed p.11

steps.title: Base pin release — TWO different mechanisms, check yours
steps.action: Uberti builds this revolver on two frames and they release the base pin differently. On the old-model or black-powder frame you loosen a base pin screw; on the new-model frame you depress a spring-loaded base pin screw. Look at your gun and identify which you have before you turn or press anything — the manual itself covers both because it cannot know which one you own.
steps.prose: Getting this wrong is how a base pin screw gets rounded off. If the screw resists turning, it is probably the spring-loaded type and wants pressing, not driving.
steps.caution: The step's second half continues on the next line as "spring-loaded base pin screw, so that the cylinder base pin can be removed from the frame by pulling it out in the direction of the muzzle."
steps.quote: 3. Depending on your model, either loosen the cylinder base pin screw or depress the
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — UNKNOWN — no revision or part code printed — Removing the Cylinder, step 3, printed p.11

steps.title: Base pin forward, cylinder out to the right
steps.action: With the pin released, draw the cylinder base pin all the way forward out of the frame toward the muzzle. Then take the cylinder out sideways through the frame window on the loading gate side.
steps.prose: The cylinder comes out the gate side and no other. Cimarron's cylinders are hand-fitted, so expect a close fit and never force it in any direction.
steps.caution: The cylinder in your revolver is hand-fitted to its frame with precision, so there likely will be a close fit.
steps.quote: 4. Slide the cylinder base pin all the way out until it is free of the frame. 5. Remove the cylinder toward the loading gate side of the revolver.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — UNKNOWN — no revision or part code printed — Removing the Cylinder, steps 4–5, printed p.11

steps.title: No steel rod on this revolver
steps.action: Pick the rod before the solvent. Uberti rules out a steel cleaning rod on this gun — use wood, aluminium or brass, with a brass bristle brush and patches sized to your calibre. Scrub each of the six cylinder chambers and the barrel bore with a good cleaning solution.
steps.prose: The bores here are not chrome lined and the forcing cone is exposed. A steel rod is what wears a crown and scores a chamber mouth.
steps.quote: To clean your revolver, use a wood, aluminum or brass cleaning rod (do not use steel), a brass bristle brush, and patches that are correctly sized to the caliber of your revolver.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — UNKNOWN — no revision or part code printed — Cleaning, printed p.11

steps.title: Brush all the way through — never reverse inside the bore
steps.action: Push the brush completely through the barrel or chamber and out the far end before you pull it back. Reversing direction while the brush is still inside is what breaks bristles off in the bore and can wedge the brush.
steps.prose: Then run clean patches through the bore and every chamber until they come out clean. That is the stopping condition, not a stroke count.
steps.quote: Always brush all the way through the bore; never try to reverse directions while the brush is actually in the barrel or chamber.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — UNKNOWN — no revision or part code printed — Cleaning, printed p.11

steps.title: Oil everything lightly, and polish the brass separately
steps.action: Once the patches come out clean, oil the whole revolver completely but lightly. The backstrap and trigger guard are solid brass and will tarnish — that comes off with any good brass polish, and it is a separate job from oiling the steel.
steps.prose: Uberti notes that oil works into the one-piece grip over the years and gives it a patina. That is the finish behaving as intended, not neglect.
steps.quote: Use a good quality brass polish on the back strap and trigger guard.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — UNKNOWN — no revision or part code printed — Cleaning, printed p.11

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The base pin is out, the cylinder is out through the gate side, and the barrel and six chambers are clean. That is the whole strip this manual publishes — the hammer, bolt, hand, springs and the hammer safety bar all appear in the parts diagram but no procedure removes any of them. Use only proper ammunition when it goes back into service.
steps.prose: Everything left in the frame is fitted work. On a hand-fitted single action that is a gunsmith's ground, not a bench job.
steps.cite: SINGLE ACTIONS, MODEL 'P', THUNDERER, LIGHTNING, MODEL 'P' JR., NEW SHERIFF, 1875, 1890 & BISLEY — UNKNOWN — no revision or part code printed — Special Safety Instructions, printed p.3

deepAbsentReason: Uberti publishes no procedure beyond removing the cylinder and base pin. The manual's only disassembly section is REMOVING THE CYLINDER (printed p.11, five steps plus reinstallation); there is no procedure anywhere in its 20 pages for the hammer, trigger, bolt, hand, sear-and-bolt spring, main spring, gate catch, ejector assembly or the hammer safety bar — all of which appear in the parts diagram on printed p.2 as identification only, exactly as a parts diagram is not a teardown. The book's own position on the fit of these parts is that the cylinder is 'hand-fitted to its frame with precision' and must never be forced, which is the same reason the fitted internals are not owner work. Cimarron's own two-page customer safety sheet, the only other document it publishes for this revolver, carries no procedure at all. Nothing beyond what the book prints has been invented.

cleaning.name: BARREL BORE
tasks: Wood, aluminium or brass rod only — never steel
Brass bristle brush and correctly sized patches, with a good cleaning solution
Brush all the way through and out; never reverse direction inside the bore
Patches through until they come out clean, then a light oil

cleaning.name: CYLINDER & CHAMBERS
tasks: Scrub each of the six chambers individually with the brush and solution
Clean the base pin bore through the centre of the cylinder
Wipe the cylinder face and the ratchet at the rear
Check the chambers are clear before it goes back in the frame

cleaning.name: FRAME, BASE PIN & GATE
tasks: Wipe fouling from the frame window, the recoil shield and the loading gate
Clean and lightly oil the base pin and its bore in the frame
Check the base pin catch plunger moves freely and returns under its own spring
Light oil over the whole revolver once it is dry

cleaning.name: BRASS FURNITURE
tasks: Backstrap and trigger guard are solid brass and will tarnish
Any good quality brass polish removes it
Keep polish off the blued steel and out of the action
Oil that works into the one-piece grip over time is expected, not damage

reassembly: Reverse the removal: cylinder in through the loading gate side of the frame, never forced from any direction.
Slide the cylinder base pin back through the frame and the cylinder from the muzzle end.
Make sure the base pin catch snaps back into place as the pin seats.
Test the catch by depressing the plunger — it must move freely and return under its own spring pressure.
Set the base pin screw to the correct notch for what you are doing: first notch for transport with the hammer at first cock, second notch for the firing position.
Close the loading gate, lower the hammer, and confirm the cylinder locks up on each chamber as the hammer is cocked.
fncheck: With the revolver empty, bring the hammer to half cock, open the gate and turn the cylinder a full revolution — it must turn freely and every chamber must be empty. Close the gate and cock the hammer through all six chambers, checking the bolt drops into each cylinder notch and locks the cylinder before the hammer reaches full cock. Depress the base pin catch plunger and confirm it returns under its own spring. Check the base pin screw is in the second notch for firing, and that the base pin safety feature is disengaged so the hammer can move fully forward. Then set it down with an empty chamber under the hammer.
